subject: Data Science
topic: Deep Learning in Data Science/Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in Image Analysis

items.title: What is a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)?
items.content: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are a type of neural network designed to analyze and understand visual data, such as images. They have been widely used in image classification, object detection, segmentation, and generation tasks.

items.title: How does a CNN perform spatial convolutions on an image?
items.content: A CNN performs spatial convolutions on an input image using kernels (small filters) that slide over the image to extract features. This process involves sliding the kernel over the image and calculating the dot product of the kernel with each pixel, resulting in feature maps.

items.title: What is the purpose of pooling layers in a CNN?
items.content: The purpose of pooling layers in a CNN is to downsample the feature maps by reducing spatial dimensions through max pooling or average pooling. This reduces the number of parameters and computational cost while preserving the most important features.

items.title: What is the difference between ReLU and Sigmoid activation functions?
items.content: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) and Sigmoid are two common activation functions used in CNNs. ReLU introduces non-linearity by clipping negative values to zero, whereas Sigmoid maps inputs to a value between 0 and 1. ReLU is commonly used due to its efficiency and effectiveness.

items.title: What is Batch Normalization used for in a CNN?
items.content: Batch Normalization normalizes the input data for each layer by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation. This improves training stability and speed by reducing internal covariate shift and making weights more robust to small changes in the input.
